newsitem.title: UK: BOXING-MARSH STEPS INTO RING FOR L.DEMOCRATS.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-MARSH STEPS INTO RING FOR L.DEMOCRATS.

text.p: Former world boxing champion Terry Marsh announced on Friday he would stand as a parliamentary candidate for Britain's Liberal Democrat Party at the next general election.
Marsh, world light-welterweight champion in the 1980s, joined the centrist Liberal Democrats early this year, after five years as a member of the main opposition Labour Party.
The ex-fireman, marine and politics student said he had made the switch because of what he called Labour's move to the centre-right of politics.
"You can hardly fit a cigarette paper between Labour and Conservative now. The Liberal Democrats are the only radical party left," he said.

He will stand in the crucial constituency of Basildon in Essex, east of London. In the 1992 election, the ruling Conservatives' ability to hang on to Basildon was the first clear indication they could win a fourth successive victory.

"I'm a role model for the people of Basildon," Marsh said. "I've lived in Basildon for 25 years. I can relate to them, and they to me." The Liberal Democrats were a distant third in Basildon in the 1992 election. Marsh, 38, was in jail on remand for 10 months before standing trial in 1990 for shooting his former boxing manager, Frank Warren. He was found not guilty.
